Reason: The CT images (Figures 1a-c) demonstrate diffuse, randomly distributed micronodules throughout the lung parenchyma, which is the hallmark radiographic appearance of miliary tuberculosis; this finding correlates clinically with systemic symptoms like prolonged fever and elevated sedimentation rate. Although the question refers to a "chest X-ray," the provided figures are axial CT slices showing the classic miliary pattern described in option B.
